subject: Biology
title: Bottleneck and Founder Effects
description: Learn Bottleneck and Founder Effects in one minute.

hook.text: Northern elephant seals were hunted to just 20 individuals. Today's population of 200,000 is genetically almost identical.

buildup.text: A population bottleneck occurs when a disaster slashes numbers, randomly eliminating most genetic diversity.

discovery.text: The founder effect happens when a small group colonizes a new area, carrying only a fraction of the original gene pool.

twist.text: Rare genetic diseases are common in some communities because their founders happened to carry those alleles.

climax.text: Cheetahs are so genetically uniform from a past bottleneck that they can accept skin grafts from any other cheetah.

punchline.text: Survival doesn't guarantee diversity. Just luck.

quiz.question: Why are cheetahs genetically almost identical?
options: A past population bottleneck eliminated most diversity
They all live in the same area

details.summary: Population bottlenecks occur when a population shrinks dramatically, randomly reducing genetic diversity regardless of allele fitness. Founder effects happen when a small group colonizes a new area, carrying only a fraction of the original population's genetic variation.
details.whyItMatters: Both effects explain why small populations have reduced genetic diversity and increased vulnerability. Cheetahs passed through a bottleneck so severe that they are nearly genetic clones, leaving them susceptible to epidemics.
takeaways: Bottlenecks randomly eliminate alleles regardless of their adaptive value
Founder effects can make rare alleles common in new populations
Reduced genetic diversity increases vulnerability to disease and inbreeding

faq.question: How do bottlenecks differ from natural selection?
faq.answer: Natural selection eliminates alleles based on fitness. Bottlenecks eliminate alleles randomly based on which individuals happen to survive. A bottleneck can remove beneficial alleles and preserve harmful ones purely by chance, unlike selection.

faq.question: Can populations recover their genetic diversity after a bottleneck?
faq.answer: Recovery is extremely slow because new variation comes only from mutation, which occurs at a low rate. Gene flow from other populations can help if they exist. Without intervention, bottlenecked populations may remain genetically impoverished for thousands of generations.
